_about: Australia's national parks with a full guide (ADR 0014), fixed by rule and checked 17 November 2026 (2026-11-17). IDs are permanent: user logs point at them. THE RULE. Every Commonwealth national park (Parks Australia lists six: Kakadu, Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa, Booderee, Christmas Island, Pulu Keeling, Norfolk Island), plus every state or territory national park that meets (a) or (b). (a) World Heritage: the park lies wholly or partly within one of Australia's 21 World Heritage properties (UNESCO, whc.unesco.org/en/statesparties/au). Properties with no state national park in them: Heard and McDonald Islands, Lord Howe Island Group (a Permanent Park Preserve), Macquarie Island (a nature reserve), Royal Exhibition Building and Carlton Gardens, Sydney Opera House; Kakadu and Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa are Commonwealth parks. Australian Convict Sites counts too: Darlington Probation Station lies in Maria Island National Park and the Old Great North Road in Dharug (and Yengo) National Park, as their agencies' pages say. CAP: where a property takes in more than eight national parks (Gondwana Rainforests of Australia, about 40 reserves; Wet Tropics of Queensland, more than 20 national parks; Great Barrier Reef, some 450 island national parks), only the parks that (i) UNESCO's own description of the property names, by the park's name or a place within it, or (ii) the managing agency's page for the property names as its principal parks. Applied: Gondwana — Wollumbin (UNESCO's Statement of Outstanding Universal Value names Wollumbin/Mt Warning) and Lamington, Springbrook, Mount Barney and Main Range (Queensland's World Heritage page: 'Discover the Gondwana Rainforests ... including Lamington, Springbrook, Mount Barney and Main Range national parks'); NSW NPWS lists its twenty Gondwana national parks without singling any out, so (ii) adds none in NSW. Wet Tropics — Daintree (the Statement names the coast 'between the Daintree River and Cedar Bay'); Queensland's list of 'some of the more popular' Wet Tropics parks names 24 and is not a principal list. Great Barrier Reef — Whitsunday Islands and Hinchinbrook Island (named in the Statement as scenic features); Lizard Island is named only as the locator of the Cod Hole and Raine Island National Park (Scientific) is closed to the public, so neither is taken. Properties with eight or fewer national parks take all of them: Greater Blue Mountains Area (seven national parks and Jenolan Karst Conservation Reserve, NSW Environment and Heritage), Tasmanian Wilderness (seven, Parks and Wildlife Service Tasmania's TWWHA page), and the rest one or two each. (b) Agency flagship: in each state and territory, the park its own agency singles out — by its visitor counts where it publishes them (NT: Parks & Wildlife NT's park visitor data, where Litchfield and Nitmiluk have each been the most-visited national park in the last five years), otherwise by a state-level claim on the agency's own page for the park (oldest, largest, most popular, iconic, favourite), quoted in 'reason'. Queensland's (Lamington) and the ACT's are covered; Lamington is already in under (a). Nambung (WA) was proposed but DBCA's page and 2024-25 annual report make no such claim for it, so it is left out. FIELDS. 'name' is the park's name as its agency writes it, with the agency's own dual-name form (Grampians (Gariwerd) National Park; Daintree National Park (CYPAL); Boodjamulla National Park (Aboriginal Land)). 'localName' only where the agency uses an Aboriginal name beside the English one and it is not already the name. 'state' is ISO 3166-2:AU, with Unigrids' own AU-JBT, AU-CX, AU-CC and AU-NF (ADR 0014). 'agency' is the managing body; Port Campbell is managed by the Great Ocean Road Coast and Parks Authority, not Parks Victoria; SA's is the Department for Environment and Water, branded National Parks and Wildlife Service South Australia. 'capadName' is the NAME in CAPAD 2024 (gis.environment.gov.au/gispubmap/rest/services/ogc_services/CAPAD/MapServer/0), which carries no type suffix (Kosciuszko, not Kosciuszko National Park); match it with a national-park TYPE and the state, since names repeat across types and states. 'capadAlsoNames' lists further CAPAD NAMEs that are the same park (Norfolk Island's two parts; Boodjamulla's handed-back Aboriginal-land part and its remainder). Daintree's NAME covers both its 'National Park' and 'National Park Aboriginal' records. 'reason' is the rule that admits the park and 'reasonSource' the page that shows it. 'passportRegion' is Unigrids' own (ADR 0014): NSW, the ACT and Jervis Bay together; the island territories together. 'jointlyManaged' is true only where an official page confirms joint or co-management with Traditional Owners (Parks Australia; NT Government plan of management; QPWS; Parks Victoria; DBCA; DEW SA; UNESCO for Mungo); CAPAD's GOVERNANCE code is not used for it. Booderee remains jointly managed while it moves to sole management by the Wreck Bay Aboriginal Community Council (target May 2028). Sources: UNESCO World Heritage Centre property pages and component lists; NSW Environment and Heritage World Heritage pages; Queensland DETSI World Heritage pages; parks.tas.gov.au; nationalparks.nsw.gov.au; parks.vic.gov.au; greatoceanroadauthority.vic.gov.au; parks.qld.gov.au; parks.sa.gov.au; exploreparks.dbca.wa.gov.au; nt.gov.au and dth.nt.gov.au; parks.act.gov.au; parksaustralia.gov.au; CAPAD 2024. Founding dates and areas are curated in each guide's facts with their source; CAPAD's GAZ_DATE is a gazettal record, not a founding date.
